newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman has "digestion problems" - state television.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman has "digestion problems" - state television.

text.p: Croatian state television on Friday played down reports that 74-year old president Franjo Tudjman was seriously ill, saying he was flown to the United States for check ups after reported digestion problems.

U.S. State department spokesman Nicholas Burns had earlier confirmed Tudjman is at Walter Reed (Army) Hospital in Bethesda, Maryland and a U.S. official told Reuters he was there for cancer treatment.

Croatian television, quoting a statement from the president's office and signed by Tudjman's private doctors, said he was treated at the Walter Reed hospital but stopped short of confirming he had cancer.

"The examination showed that problems were caused by gastric ulcer and swollen lymph nodules in the stomach," the television said in its 14th domestic item, half an hour into the main evening bulletin.
"The President is feeling well, and is performing his duties. He will be returning to the country by the end of next week," it added.
The Croatian state-run news agency HINA reported on Wednesday that Tudjman had taken a short break for a "regular medical check-up."
Croatian officials were not available for comments on Friday evening.
The news came as a surprise as Tudjman sought to project an image of a healthy, energetic man, often shown on television playing tennis.
He appeared in public for the last time last Thursday when he presided over a government session dedicated to the country's admission to the Council of Europe. He looked pale and had sunken cheeks.

Tudjman is one of the three key players in the U.S.-sponsored Dayton peace deal that brought peace to Bosnia after a 43-month old war, together with Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and Alija Izetbegovic of Bosnia.
He and Milosevic normalised relations last August, shoring up the peace process in the Balkans.
Croatia's constitution envisages that if the president is incapacitated, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, a post currently occupied by Vlatko Pavletic, would take over.
